section_summary: This section covers U.S. State Department records from 1941 to 1944 concerning the proceedings, reorganization, and legislative actions of the Japanese Imperial Diet during World War II. It details the Diet's 76th, 81st, 83rd, and 85th sessions, focusing on wartime mobilization laws, record budget appropriations, the dissolution of traditional political parties, and controversies surrounding the Imperial Rule Assistance Association. Reports and intelligence analyses from Tokyo, Buenos Aires, Chungking, Moscow, and Washington trace the centralization of executive power under Prime Minister Hideki Tojo and monitor Japan's political and military posture toward Southeast Asia and the Soviet Union.

subfiles.about: Concluding remarks of an official address addressing the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, the Three-Power Pact, and honoring the Japanese armed forces.
subfiles.summary: Conclusion of an address calling for ending the war and a Greater East Asia sphere of common prosperity, confident in the Three Power Pact, with tributes to fallen soldiers.
subfiles.title: Address on Greater East Asia and the Three-Power Pact (Conclusion)

subfiles.about: Reports on a secret session of both houses of the Japanese Diet regarding the Thailand-Indochina mediation, international situation, and the China incident.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports both Diet houses met in secret session March 15, 1941 to hear ministers on Thailand-Indochina mediation, the international situation and the China incident.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 413: Diet Secret Session on Thailand-Indochina Mediation and China Incident

subfiles.about: Reports the formal close of the 76th Diet session, summarizing legislative accomplishments and domestic press criticism regarding party politics and foreign opportunities.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the 76th Diet closed March 26, 1941 after approving a budget over 13 billion yen and 87 bills; editorials praise speed but fault party loyalties and see opportunity in the Netherlands East Indies.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 464: Closing of the 76th Diet Session and Press Comment

subfiles.about: Summarizes Tokyo Despatch No. 5496 regarding procedural changes, legislative compromises, and key mobilization bills during the 76th Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Schmidt's memorandum on Despatch No. 5496: interpellations were dropped for withdrawal of controversial bills, mobilization measures passed and terms extended a year; the Diet showed it was not wholly totalitarian.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Division Memorandum: Analysis of Despatch No. 5496 on the 76th Diet Session

subfiles.about: Comprehensive report on the organization, legislative proceedings, political compromises, and constitutional role of the 76th session of the Imperial Diet.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew provides an extensive report analyzing the 76th session of the Imperial Diet, which formally closed on March 26, 1941. Operating for the first time without formal political parties, the Diet agreed to abandon plenary interpellations, while Premier Konoe's Cabinet dropped roughly half of its scheduled legislative bills and extended parliamentary terms by one year. The report highlights contentious debates over the budget and organization of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association, notes sidelights such as Konoe's politically convenient illness, and reviews discussions on Oceania and Thailand-Indochina mediation. Grew concludes that while the Diet was compliant, its jealous defense of constitutional prerogatives demonstrated that parliamentary traditions had not been completely extinguished.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 5496: Seventy-Sixth Session of the Japanese Diet

subfiles.about: Reports Japanese press editorials urging the convocation of a special Diet session following the Imperial Conference of July 2, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Tokyo papers urging an August special Diet session after the July 2 Imperial Conference to unify the nation and clarify policy on the German-Soviet war.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 982: Press Urges Convocation of a Special Diet Session

subfiles.about: Details the opening schedule, agenda, and legislative program of the extraordinary Diet session convened by the Tojo Cabinet in November 1941.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the Tojo Cabinet's extraordinary Diet session of November 15, 1941, with ministerial speeches, interpellations, and measures on military service, budgets and tax increases.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 1806: Convening of Extraordinary Diet Session Under the Tojo Cabinet

subfiles.about: Records FBIS monitored radio reports indicating a postponement of the Diet reconvening scheduled for January 21, 1943, and its connection to Premier Tojo.
subfiles.summary: Benninghoff relays monitored Tokyo broadcasts that the January 21 Diet reconvening was postponed, linked vaguely to Tojo; such delays usually meant serious internal crises.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Division Memorandum: Postponement of Diet Reconvening

subfiles.about: Reports on Domei news coverage of the 81st Diet's secret sessions, naval victory announcements off Rennell Island, and Premier Tojo's address on Asian independence.
subfiles.from: First Secretary of Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.summary: Buenos Aires report on the 81st Diet reconvening January 28, 1943: secret Lower House sessions, 88 bills, a 2.3 billion yen supplementary budget, and Tojo's promise of independence for Burma, India and the Philippines.
subfiles.title: Buenos Aires C.I.O. Report No. 8552: Japanese Eighty-First Diet Reconvenes Mainly to Pass Budget Measures

subfiles.about: Assesses whether the extraordinary Diet session convened by Premier Tojo in June 1943 presaged an imminent Japanese attack on the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: Benninghoff refutes speculation that the June 15, 1943 special Diet session prepared war against the Soviet Union, citing its focus on wartime economic controls and stable Moscow-Tokyo relations.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Division Memorandum: The Special Session of the Japanese Diet and Soviet-Japanese Relations

subfiles.about: Analyzes the proceedings, executive powers, and legislative output of the 81st Diet session, enclosing a comprehensive list of 89 passed bills.
subfiles.summary: A comprehensive intelligence study prepared by H. Merrell Benninghoff based on FBIS radio monitoring of the 81st Diet session, which ran from December 1942 to March 1943 following a postponement attributed to Premier Tojo's illness. Having been elected through the IRAA recommendation system in May 1942, the Diet acted largely as a compliant body, approving a 39.34 billion yen budget and passing controversial ordinances granting the Premier unprecedented direct control over cabinet ministers and war industries. The memorandum also examines contentious debate over the Special Wartime Criminal Law curbing press freedom, local government administration reforms, and includes an extensive three-page list detailing 89 specific legislative acts passed during the session.
subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs Division Memorandum: The 81st Session of the Japanese Diet (December 1942-March 1943)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Chungking Despatch No. 1365 transmitting a memorandum on the significance of the June 1943 extraordinary Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Chungking Despatch No. 1365 (July 20, 1943) enclosing a memorandum on the significance of the June 16-18, 1943 extraordinary Diet session.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Chungking Despatch No. 1365: Significance of Extraordinary Session of Japanese Diet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet indexing Moscow Telegram No. 2034 regarding a Soviet press article analyzing the 83rd Extraordinary Session of the Japanese Parliament.

subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Harriman's Moscow Telegram No. 2034 (November 24, 1943) reporting A. Ilin's article on the 83rd Extraordinary Japanese Diet session.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Moscow Telegram No. 2034: Soviet Commentary on the 83rd Extraordinary Diet Session

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet (with duplicate copy on page 106) indexing Moscow Telegram No. 3016 on a Japanese Cabinet resolution calling the 85th Extraordinary Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference, in two identical copies, to Moscow Telegram No. 3016 (August 16, 1944): the Japanese Cabinet resolved to convene the 85th Extraordinary Diet session.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet on Moscow Telegram No. 3016: Resolution Calling 85th Extraordinary Session of Parliament
